entries.citation: de Leva P (1996). Adjustments to Zatsiorsky-Seluyanov's segment inertia parameters. Journal of Biomechanics 29(9):1223-1230.
entries.retrieval: The primary PDF copy found (ebm.ufabc.edu.br/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/Leva-1996.pdf) failed TLS certificate verification and was not opened; the Elsevier copy is paywalled. Values below come from the transcription in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/main/src/shared/python/body_segment_parameters/data/de_leva_1996_table4.json (retrieved 2026-11-01, sha256 f9afb52b883ede994b1048f8b759611a890b20af663287921290e30cbda104c4), which states 'Table 4 (page 1228), both parts: easy-to-use endpoints and alternative endpoints', 'values exactly as printed'. Cross-checks: (1) the SimTK lab entry (simtk_lab_deleva) reproduces every primary female row from an independent computation; (2) the alternative rows reproduce the primary rows' physical quantities in millimetres (head CM 0.4841 x 243.7 = 118.0 mm = 0.5894 x 200.2; upper-trunk CM below CERV 0.505 x 228.0 = 115.1 mm = (228.0 - 142.5) + 0.2077 x 142.5; head sagittal radius 0.271 x 243.7 = 66.0 mm = 0.330 x 200.2; upper-trunk radii 106.2/71.6/102.4 mm by either row), which a transcription slip would break.

values.conditions: Zatsiorsky-Seluyanov female sample as adjusted by de Leva

values.units: mm; % body mass; % of length from origin (VERT); radii % of length
values.conditions: female; head segment includes the neck (trunk starts at CERV or SUPR); adjusted
female; marked unadjusted (*) in the transcription
female; adjusted; MIDS = mid-point of the shoulder joint centres

values.value: radii of gyration about the sagittal (antero-posterior), transverse (medio-lateral) and longitudinal axes
values.conditions: stated in the transcription's conventions; the SimTK lab assigns r_sag to I_xx with x along the antero-posterior axis; the trunk rows require it (upper trunk r_sag 74.6 > r_trans 50.2 because the trunk is wider than deep)

mismatches: Head centre of mass: model takes 58.94% (the VERT-MIDG row's value) of the VERT-CERV length (243.7 mm row); the coherent VERT-CERV value is 48.41%. At 1.64 m the model's head CM sits 0.1358 m below the vertex; de Leva puts it 0.1115 m below, 24 mm higher.

Head radii of gyration: model applies the VERT-MIDG percentages (35.9, 33.0, 31.8) to the VERT-CERV length; the coherent VERT-CERV percentages are 27.1 sagittal, 29.5 transverse, 26.1 longitudinal. With the axis swap below, the model's head inertias are x 1.75, y 1.25, z 1.48 times de Leva's.

Thorax (upper trunk) centre of mass: model takes 20.77% (the SUPR-XYPH row's value, measured from SUPR) of the CERV-XYPH length (228.0 mm row) measured from CERV; the coherent value is 50.50% of CERV-XYPH from CERV. At 1.64 m the model's thorax CM sits 0.0448 m below CERV; de Leva puts it 0.1088 m below, 64 mm lower.

Thorax radii of gyration: model applies the SUPR-XYPH percentages (74.6, 50.2, 71.8) to the 228.0 mm length; the coherent CERV-XYPH percentages are 46.6 sagittal, 31.4 transverse, 44.9 longitudinal. With the axis swap, the model's thorax inertias are x 1.16, y 5.64, z 2.56 times de Leva's.

Sagittal and transverse radii are exchanged for every segment: model.py puts r_trans about x (forward) and r_sag about y (left). Ratios of model to de Leva inertia (x, y): abdomen 0.67, 1.50; pelvis 0.86, 1.16; upper arm 0.87, 1.14; thigh 0.97, 1.03; shank 0.97, 1.03. For the foot, whose long axis is x, de Leva's r_sag (29.9) belongs about the vertical axis z and r_trans (27.9) about y; the model has y 29.9, z 27.9. For the forearm and hand the exchange suits the model's rest pose, whose palms face the thighs (90 degrees of pronation from the palm-forward anatomical position in which the data are defined), so those two can stay as they are with a note.

Foot and toes centre of mass: the foot (1.00%) and toes (0.29%) combine at 0.114 m from the heel, 49.6% of the 0.230 m heel-toe length (heel at x = -0.050 m, as the toe-tip formula implies); de Leva's 40.14% puts it 0.092 m from the heel, 22 mm further back.
Comments in model.py lines 113 and 131 describe the thorax CM as '20.77% from CERV' and the head CM as '58.94% of VERT-CERV'; both percentages belong to the other endpoint rows.
model_comparison.agreements: Segment lengths are Table 4 lengths for the endpoints used (VERT-CERV 243.7, CERV-XYPH 228.0, XYPH-OMPH 205.3, OMPH-MIDH 181.5, SJC-EJC 275.1, EJC-WJC 264.3, WJC-MET3 78.0, HJC-KJC 368.5, KJC-LMAL 432.3, scaled by 1.64/1.735). Mass shares sum to 99.99% and match Table 4 (neck 1.00% taken from the head and 0.40% per clavicle from the upper trunk are recorded placements). CM percentages for MPT, LPT, upper arm, forearm, hand, thigh and shank match. The foot length 0.230 m is a recorded choice (de Leva scaled gives 0.216 m).
model_comparison.consequence_for_turns: calculation: whole-body moment of inertia about the vertical axis through the CoM in the rest pose, from model.py's segments, is 0.701 kg m^2; with de Leva's coherent thorax and head longitudinal radii it is 0.578 kg m^2 (18% lower). A turn with a given angular momentum spins about 21% faster with the corrected values.
